findings.explanation: verifySignature() fails OPEN: when fbAppSecret is not configured, every POST to /webhook is accepted as authentic with zero validation of who sent it. index.js only logs a warning and keeps running (FB_APP_SECRET check at index.js:570 does not exit), so in any deployment where the env var is missing/misconfigured, a stranger can POST arbitrary JSON that flows straight into handleEvent() as if it were a real Messenger event.

body = req.body is used with no null/type guard. If the request bypasses signature checks (see line 266 finding) and is sent with a non-JSON Content-Type, express.json() never populates req.body and it stays undefined, so body.object throws inside this async route handler. There is no try/catch around the handler and no global unhandledRejection guard in index.js, so the request hangs with no response and, on Node >=15 default settings, the whole process can be terminated.

body.entry || [] only guards against a falsy value; it does not check Array.isArray(). A payload like {"object":"page","entry":{}} passes body.object === 'page' and reaches this line, where for...of on a non-iterable object throws 'is not iterable' with no surrounding try/catch — same unhandled-rejection risk as the line 542 finding.

entry (an element of the attacker-controlled body.entry array) is accessed as entry.messaging with no optional chaining; entry: null in the payload throws immediately. Even when entry is an object, entry.messaging || [] again skips Array.isArray(), so entry.messaging being a non-array truthy value (string/object) also throws 'is not iterable'. Both crash the unguarded async handler rather than being rejected as a clean 400.

inferBaseUrlFromRequest builds the base URL straight from the client-supplied X-Forwarded-Proto/X-Forwarded-Host headers (and the plain Host header at line 303 as fallback) with no allowlist/validation. The HMAC signature only covers the raw body, never these headers, so this value is effectively unauthenticated. It is passed as baseUrlOverride into getMenuImageUrls/buildRequestedImageUrls and ends up embedded in image URLs sent out via sendImage — a header-injection surface that should be validated against a known host instead of trusted verbatim.
